59688-chiricahua-national-monument-1958.creator: Unknown
59688-chiricahua-national-monument-1958.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ptions ceased, and were followed by movements in the earth's crust which slowly lifted and tilted great rock masses to form mountains. The stresses responsible for the movements caused a definite pattern of vertical cracks. Storms and other agencies of erosion, especially running water carrying small particles of rock, immediately set to work on the long, slow task of wearing down these mountains.

arxiv-1710-08350.title: Algebra, coalgebra, and minimization in polynomial differential equations
arxiv-1710-08350.creator: Michele Boreale
arxiv-1710-08350.description: Abstract . We consider reasoning and minimization in systems of polynomial ordinary differential equations ( ode ’s). The ring of multivariate polynomials is employed as a syntax for denoting system behaviours. We endow this set with a transition system structure based on the concept of Lie derivative , thus inducing a notion of ℒ \mathcal{L} - bisimulation .

arxiv-2107-08865.title: Ab Initio Particle-based Object Manipulation
arxiv-2107-08865.creator: Siwei Chen, Xiao Ma, Yunfan Lu and David Hsu
arxiv-2107-08865.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Siwei Chen, Xiao Ma, Yunfan Lu and David Hsu. Particle-based Object Manipulation ( PROMPT ) is a new method for robot manipulation of novel objects, without prior object models or pre-training on a large object data set. The key element of PROMPT is a particle-based object representation, in which each particle represents a point in an object, the local geometric, physical, and other features of the point, and also its relation with other particles. The particle representation connects visual perception with robot control.

arxiv-2206-04290.title: Stability of Certain Higher Degree Polynomials
arxiv-2206-04290.creator: Shanta Laishram, Ritumoni Sarma, Himanshu Sharma
arxiv-2206-04290.description: Abstract . One of the interesting problems in arithmetic dynamics is to study the stability of polynomials over a field. In this paper, we study the stability of f ⁡ ( z ) = z d + 1 c f(z)=z^{d}+\frac{1}{c} for d ≥ 2 d\geq 2 , c ∈ ℤ ∖ { 0 } c\in{\mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}} .

arxiv-2211-13957.title: Probability Distribution Functions of Sunspot Magnetic Flux Journal: ApJ Facilities: SDO(HMI), SOHO(MDI), Hinode(SOT), KPNO
arxiv-2211-13957.creator: Takashi Sakurai, Shin Toriumi
arxiv-2211-13957.description: Abstract We have investigated the probability distributions of sunspot area and magnetic flux by using the data from Royal Greenwich Observatory and USAF/NOAA. We have constructed a sample of 2995 regions with maximum-development areas ≥ \geq 500 MSH (millionths of solar hemisphere), covering 146.7 years (1874–2020).

arxiv-2407-07937.title: Rising from the ashes: evidence of old stellar populations and rejuvenation events in the very early Universe 2024 Rising from the ashes: evidence of old stellar populations and rejuvenation events in the very early Universe – 12
arxiv-2407-07937.creator: Callum Witten, William McClymont, Nicolas Laporte, Guido Roberts-Borsani, Debora Sijacki, Sandro Tacchella, Charlotte Simmonds, Harley Katz, Richard S. Ellis, Joris Witstok, Roberto Maiolino, Xihan Ji, Billy R. Hayes, Tobias J. Looser, Francesco D’Eugenio
arxiv-2407-07937.description: Abstract While JWST has observed galaxies assembling as early as z ∼ 14 z\sim 14 , evidence of galaxies with significant old stellar populations in the Epoch of Reionisation (EoR) – the descendants of these earliest galaxies – are few and far between.

arxiv-2507-02562.title: Multi-Utterance Speech Separation and Association Trained on Short Segments
arxiv-2507-02562.description: Abstract Current deep neural network (DNN) based speech separation faces a fundamental challenge — while the models need to be trained on short segments due to computational constraints, real-world applications typically require processing significantly longer recordings with multiple utterances per speaker than seen during training.

arxiv-2508-00527.title: Evolutionary learning of microbial populations in partially predictable environments
arxiv-2508-00527.creator: Roaa Mohmmed Yagb Omer, Onofrio Mazzarisi, Martina Dal Bello, Jacopo Grilli
arxiv-2508-00527.description: Abstract Populations evolving in fluctuating environments face the fundamental challenge of balancing adaptation to current conditions against preparation for uncertain futures. Here, we study microbial evolution in partially predictable environments using proteome allocation models that capture the trade-off between growth rate and lag time during environmental transitions.

arxiv-2509-16820.title: DISCO: Disentangled Communication Steering for Large Language Models
arxiv-2509-16820.creator: Max Torop, Aria Masoomi, Masih Eskandar, Jennifer Dy
arxiv-2509-16820.description: Abstract A variety of recent methods guide large language model outputs via the inference-time addition of steering vectors to residual-stream or attention-head representations. In contrast, we propose to inject steering vectors directly into the query and value representation spaces within attention heads.

arxiv-2509-24487.title: Finding rare classes in large datasets: the case of polluted white dwarfs from Gaia XP spectra
arxiv-2509-24487.creator: Xander Byrne, 1 Amy Bonsor, 1 Laura K. Rogers, 2,1 Mariona Badenas-Agusti 1 1 Institute of Astronomy, University of Cambridge, Madingley Road, Cambridge CB3 0HA, UK 2 NOIRLab, 950 N Cherry Ave, Tucson, AZ, 85719, USA
arxiv-2509-24487.description: Abstract The Gaia mission’s third data release recorded low-resolution spectra for about 100 000 100\,000 white dwarf candidates. A small subset of these spectra show evidence of characteristic broad Ca ii absorption features, implying the accretion of rocky material by so-called polluted white dwarfs – important probes of the composition of exoplanetary material.

arxiv-2601-08194.title: From Fixed to Flexible: Shaping AI Personality in Context-Sensitive Interaction CCS: Human-centered computing Empirical studies in interaction design CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI) CCS: Human-centered computing HCI design and evaluation methods
arxiv-2601-08194.creator: Shakyani Jayasiriwardene, Hongyu Zhou, Weiwei Jiang, Benjamin Tag, Emmanuel Stamatakis, Anusha Withana, Zhanna Sarsenbayeva
arxiv-2601-08194.description: Abstract . Conversational agents are increasingly expected to adapt across contexts and evolve their personalities through interactions, yet most remain static once configured. We present an exploratory study of how user expectations form and evolve when agent personality is made dynamically adjustable.

arxiv-2601-18465.title: Spontaneous epicuticular charging affects droplet dynamics on living leaves
arxiv-2601-18465.creator: Mihir Durve, Serena Armiento, Benham Kamare, Sauro Succi, Barbara Mazzolai, Fabian Meder
arxiv-2601-18465.description: Abstract 1 Abstract How water droplets move and slide on leaves influences plant ecophysiological and abiotic interactions [ 28 , 15 , 43 , 42 ] , as well as the design of advanced bio-inspired wetting materials [ 25 , 26 , 18 ] .

arxiv-2602-17694.title: AsynDBT: Asynchronous Distributed Bilevel Tuning for efficient In-Context Learning with Large Language Models
arxiv-2602-17694.creator: Hui Ma, Shaoyu Dou, Ya Liu, Fei Xing, Li Feng, Feng Pi
arxiv-2602-17694.description: Abstract With the rapid development of large language models (LLMs), an increasing number of applications leverage cloud-based LLM APIs to reduce usage costs. However, since cloud-based models’ parameters and gradients are agnostic, users have to manually or use heuristic algorithms to adjust prompts for intervening LLM outputs, which requiring costly optimization procedures.

arxiv-2603-23894.title: Latin squares with non-partitioning disjoint subsquares
arxiv-2603-23894.creator: Tara Kemp

doe-osti-3388418-transmittal-of-surveill.creator: DeAguero, Anna
doe-osti-3388418-transmittal-of-surveill.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. On 4/14/2026, the surveillance team leader accompanied the LANL NNSS Waste Certification Program's alternate waste certification official (AWCO) to TA-03 Building 102 northeast end to observe NNSS shipment #LAL26029 to NNSS for disposal.

pmc-10648032.title: Design of an Artificial Intelligence of Things-Based Sesame Oil Evaluator for Quality Assessment Using Gas Sensors and Deep Learning Mechanisms
pmc-10648032.creator: Hao-Hsiang Ku, Ching-Fu Lung, Ching-Ho Chi, Wenjing Cui
pmc-10648032.description: Traditional oil quality measurement is mostly based on chemical indicators such as acid value, peroxide value, and p-anisidine value. This process requires specialized knowledge and involves complex steps. Hence, this study designs and proposes a Sesame Oil Quality Assessment Service Platform, which is composed of an Intelligent Sesame Oil Evaluator (ISO Evaluator) and a Cloud Service Platform.

pmc-11354736.title: Population Dynamics of Bactrocera dorsalis (Diptera: Tephritidae) in Four Counties of Yunnan, China, by Electronic Monitoring System
pmc-11354736.creator: Ziyuan Li, Yan Li, Yuling Liang, Yixiang Qi, Yongyue Lu, Jiao Ma, Lukasz L Stelinski
pmc-11354736.description: Simple SummaryBactrocera dorsalis (Hendel) is a serious threat to the fruit industry. Implementing monitoring procedures is essential for effective pest control. The monitoring of B. dorsalis is predominantly conducted through the use of yellow sticky traps and baited traps, followed by manual counting. However, this approach is both time consuming and labor intensive.

pmc-11517995.title: Barriers to Cardiac Rehabilitation Enrollment and Secondary Prevention Adherence in Patients with Coronary Heart Disease Following Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: A Cross-sectional Survey
pmc-11517995.creator: Ahmed M Almoghairi, Jane O’Brien, Anna Doubrovsky, Jed Duff
pmc-11517995.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate adherence to secondary prevention measures and to identify barriers to cardiac rehabilitation enrolment among patients with coronary heart disease after percutaneous coronary intervention.MethodsAn observational cross-sectional survey was conducted through computer-assisted telephone interviews to assess recently treated percutaneous coronary intervention patients at the Prince Sultan Cardiac Center in Saudi Arabia.

pmc-11657095.title: Digitalization in the operating theatre- an interview study of operating room nurses’ and nurse anesthetists’ experiences in Norway
pmc-11657095.creator: Ann-Chatrin Linqvist Leonardsen, Vivian Nystrøm, Anne Kristin Hole Trollnes, Renate Slang, Eilen Olsen
pmc-11657095.description: BackgroundDigitalization in the health sector requires adaptive change in human attitudes and skills. The operating theatres have been introduced to digital innovations through centuries. The aim of this study was to explore operating room (OR) nurses’ and Nurse Anesthetists’ (NAs) experiences with digitalization in the operating theatre.

pmc-11662402.title: Transient pacing pulse on the T-wave: What is the mechanism?
pmc-11662402.creator: Yuta Sudo
pmc-11662402.description: A patient with a dual-chamber pacemaker for sick sinus syndrome was hospitalized for heart failure. The electrocardiography (ECG) during hospitalization displayed seemingly abnormal pacing artifacts. This report focuses on the problem-solving of an abnormal-looking paced ECG and identifies the pacemaker's operational behavior as the underlying reason.

pmc-11713052.title: FTD Disorders Registry (FTDDR) Participants: Understanding Social Risk Factors in Research Participation
pmc-11713052.creator: Sweatha Reddy, Robert Reinecker, Carrie Milliard, Hilary W. Heuer, Leah K. Forsberg, Adam L. Boxer, Howard J. Rosen, Brad F. Boeve
pmc-11713052.description: BackgroundFrontotemporal degeneration (FTD) is an umbrella term encompassing a range of rare neurodegenerative disorders that cause progressive changes to behavior, personality, language, and movement with onset typically before age 60. Currently, several potential FTD therapies are under investigation, underscoring the need for increased diversity in research participation.

pmc-12653580.title: Impact of a High-Fat High-Carbohydrate (HFHC) Diet at a Young Age on Steroid Hormone Hair Concentrations in Mice: A Comparison with a Control Diet and Nutraceutical Supplementation
pmc-12653580.creator: Isabella Pividori, Tanja Peric, Antonella Comin, Natalia Rosso, Silvia Gazzin, Mirco Corazzin, Alberto Prandi, Georg Kranz
pmc-12653580.description: An unhealthy prepubertal diet can have long-lasting effects throughout life. This study investigated hair concentrations of adrenal and sex steroids, in an in vivo mouse model of juvenile obesity subjected to control (CTRL), obesogenic (HFHC) diet, or nutraceutical supplementation (silymarin or coconut oil) diets.

pmc-12739860.title: The prolonged devastation of climate change on public health in Somalia: a silent crisis
pmc-12739860.creator: Saadaq Adan Hussein, Marian Muse Osman, Mohamed Mohamoud Hassan, Yahye Sheikh Abdulle Hassan, Abdirahman Aden Hussein, Rage Adem, Mohamed M. Ali Fuje, Abdinur Hussein Mohamed, Ayan Nur Ali, Khadar Hussein Mohamud, Abdirahman Moallim Ibrahim, AbdulJalil Abdullahi Ali
pmc-12739860.description: IntroductionSomalia, one of the world’s most climate-vulnerable nations despite contributing minimally to global emissions, is facing escalating public health crises due to climate change. Rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, recurrent droughts, and floods have intensified food insecurity, disease outbreaks, and population displacement.

pmc-13255392.title: Posterior occupancy ratio–guided anterior cervical discectomy and fusion combined with unilateral biportal endoscopic decompression for pincer-type cervical spondylotic myelopathy: a case report and literature review
pmc-13255392.creator: Chuxi Wang, Hongjie Zhang, Ziwei Yu, Yingzi Liao, Wei Chen, Jiafang Zhang
pmc-13255392.description: BackgroundPincer-type cervical spondylotic myelopathy (CSM) represents a severe clinical phenotype characterized by simultaneous spinal cord compression from both ventral and dorsal structures, frequently necessitating circumferential decompression. Although traditional single-stage combined anterior-posterior (A-P) open surgery provides adequate decompression, it is often associated with extensive surgical trauma and an elevated risk of perioperative complications.

pmc-13274511.title: Correlation Between Screen Time, Sleep Duration, and Stroop Effect Among First-Year Osteopathic Medical Students: A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13274511.creator: Raju Panta, Pedro Del Corral, Summer Hales, Piercarla Fernandez, Emily Ahearn, Mark Parsamian
pmc-13274511.description: Background: The Stroop test is a well‑validated measure of selective attention and inhibitory control. Although increased electronic device use has been consistently associated with shorter sleep duration and delayed bedtime, whether everyday variability in screen time and sleep relates to Stroop performance in medical trainees remains uncertain, and existing findings on executive function are mixed.

pmc-13543875.title: Limitations of evaluating risks of all cancers combined in etiological epidemiology research
pmc-13543875.creator: Julie E Goodman, Satori A Marchitti, Nicole S Olgun, David L Eaton
pmc-13543875.description: The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) was the first public health agency to conclude that an agent – in this case, 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (TCDD) – could be carcinogenic based on associations with all cancers combined, even though there were no consistent associations with any particular cancer type. Most types of cancer each represent an etiologically distinct disease.
